summary: Reviewed the selected operator selu_ (subject cec7c025...) end to end: the frozen catalog Definition, oracle, 24 correctness and 12 timing workloads, the evaluation contract, the optimize ledger plus its best kernel (round 1), and the review_tests evidence. The best kernel (.best_kernel.py, identical to best_code in the ledger/optimize output) is a genuine FlagGems-style in-place Triton implementation: it computes scale*where(x>0, x, alpha*(exp(x)-1)) in fp32 and casts back to the input dtype, stores to the same pointer (no aliasing violation), returns the same tensor, defines run(A) with the Definition's parameter name, and contains no torch.ops.aten / torch.selu_ fallback, no dispatcher or reference replacement, no host synchronization and no environment mutation. Mutation + return-alias effects declared in definition.json are honoured. The candidate validated 36/36 workloads with abs_err/rel_err 0.0, so correctness is not in question for the frozen case set. Two substantive code limitations remain: (a) the non-contiguous path decomposes only 4 padded dimensions, so rank>4 non-contiguous inputs compute wrong offsets (torch.selu_ supports arbitrary rank); (b) the candidate is slower than the reference on every one of the 12 timing workloads (geo_mean 0.1271, min speedup 0.0820, 6.5x-12.2x slower), and the profile-measured BLOCK_SIZE=8192 retune (605 -> 176 us on 4096x4096) was never adopted. The review_tests stage recorded an explicit orchestration skip for a different subject sha (9f57f199...), so no test-contract review of this candidate exists; I reviewed the Definition/oracle/workloads directly instead and found no candidate-injection or reference-circularity defect. All code findings are advisory per policy.

findings.evidence: .best_kernel.py:87-93 defines _padded_4d() which only pads rank<4 shapes with leading size-1 dims and returns rank>4 shapes unchanged; .best_kernel.py:123-138 then passes only shape[0..3]/strides[0..3] to selu_kernel_strided, whose index decomposition (.best_kernel.py:67-74: d3=idx%s3, d2=r%s2, d1=r%s1, d0=r//s1) therefore covers at most 4 dimensions. selu_kernel_strided is selected for every non-contiguous input (.best_kernel.py:117,123). The catalog Definition (definition.json:4-22) constrains only the parameter A, with no rank limit, and the reference is torch.selu_ (oracle.py:74-76), which handles arbitrary rank. Frozen workloads never exceed rank 2 (correctness.jsonl:1-24 shapes [0],[1],[1025],[7,9]; timing.jsonl:1-12 shapes [1024],[65536],[1048576],[4096,4096]), so the shipped evaluations do not exercise this path.
findings.reason: For a non-contiguous tensor of rank >= 5 the candidate decomposes the linear index over only 4 of the dimensions, so higher-order digit d0 exceeds s0 and offs can address beyond the tensor's numel; the result is silently wrong values and a possible out-of-bounds device access. That is a semantic deviation from the declared torch.selu_ ABI (which accepts any rank), even though the frozen workloads do not cover it. Purely contiguous rank>=5 inputs are unaffected because they take the fast path at .best_kernel.py:117-121. Relatedly, the kernel always upcasts to fp32 (.best_kernel.py:39,78), so float64 inputs would lose precision relative to torch.selu_; no fp64 workload exists in the contract, so that part is advisory only.
findings.requested_change: Make the non-contiguous path rank-correct: either collapse to a <=4D view (e.g. handle a contiguous sub-block / x.contiguous()-style copy for rank>4 non-contiguous inputs) or generalize the decomposition to N dims, and fail loudly rather than silently mis-index if an unsupported layout is detected. Do not change the contiguous fast path or the arithmetic, and re-verify the existing 24 correctness cases plus a rank-5 non-contiguous case.

findings.evidence: .ledger.json:42-53 (round-1 evaluation: geo_mean 0.13037, min_speedup 0.08190, worst selu_-timing-11 at 0.60199 ms vs reference 0.04930 ms) and .ledger.json:476-486 (/ 357-486 per-workload timings) show the candidate slower than the reference on all 12 timing workloads; optimize_definition_output.json:4-6 and :14-205 give the final verification geo_mean 0.12709 with speedups 0.082-0.155 (e.g. timing-0 0.07499 ms vs 0.01159 ms = 6.5x slower; timing-11 0.60199 ms vs 0.04930 ms = 12.2x slower). .ledger.json:506 attributes the 75 us floor on 9 of 12 workloads to per-call host dispatch (logger.debug at .best_kernel.py:97, kwargs dispatch chain at :99-110, a lambda grid rebuilt per call at :118/:124, torch_device_fn.device context per call at :119/:125) versus ~11.6 us for torch.selu_, and the 4096x4096 case to a 16384-program grid of 1024-element blocks; .ledger.json:215 and :508 record that a BLOCK_SIZE=8192 tile was measured at 605 -> 176 us but was not adopted, and round 2's cached-launch attempt silently fell back to the stock launch (.ledger.json:1452) so the final code is unchanged from round 1.
findings.reason: The accepted best kernel is a substantial performance regression against the reference it is measured against (geometric mean ~7.9x slower; worst workload 12.2x), so the optimization stage produced no usable speedup. The known, already-measured fixes (larger BLOCK_SIZE / grid-stride loop for the issue-bound 4096x4096 grid, and removing per-call Python dispatch work) were identified but never landed. Correctness is unaffected (36/36 passed, abs/rel error 0.0). This is a quality/optimization finding, not a correctness or contract violation, and is advisory.
findings.requested_change: Apply the measured BLOCK_SIZE retune (e.g. 8192 or a grid-stride loop) for the large grids and trim the per-call host path (drop logger.debug, precompute the grid tuple, hoist the device guard), then re-measure all 12 timing workloads. Any cached-launch scheme must be validated in-process (assert the compiled handle lookup hits and exactly one kernel launch occurs) before it is credited, as the round-2 lesson in .ledger.json:1456 states.

findings.evidence: correctness.jsonl:1-3,8-10,17-18 contain 6 of 24 correctness cases with shape [0] (float16, bfloat16 and float32, both strided and non-strided), all satisfied trivially by the early return at .best_kernel.py:112-114; the only non-empty shapes are [1], [1025] and [7,9], i.e. rank <= 2, so the strided kernel's multi-dimension digit decomposition is only checked on a padded 1D/2D layout. timing.jsonl:1-12 times only contiguous tensors, so the non-contiguous path is never measured. Total case count is 24 < 100 (evaluate.json:15 reports 36 workloads: 24 correctness + 12 timing).
findings.reason: A quarter of the correctness budget is spent on degenerate empty tensors that cannot detect any kernel defect, and no case exercises rank >= 3 or the strided path under timing. This is a limitation of the case list itself, not of the candidate; it is advisory for the pytest/source owner and does not block anything.
findings.requested_change: Record for pytest review (non-blocking): add non-empty rank>=3 shapes and, if the source suite has them, a non-contiguous timing case; optionally replace some shape-[0] cases with non-empty small shapes so the case budget exercises the kernels.
